close_reason: Done — AvailabilityError now has thiserror-derived Display/Error + #[non_exhaustive]
description:
crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:235-247 defines:

```rust
pub enum AvailabilityError<E: std::error::Error> {
    Backend(E),
    InvalidRequest(String),
    // ...
}
```

The enum derives only `Debug` and is parameterized over `E: std::error::Error`, but no `impl std::fmt::Display` or `impl std::error::Error` is provided.

Today its only call site (principal.rs:91-95) destructures variants directly so nothing forces these impls. But:
- Any caller using `?` to forward the error needs Display + Error to convert
- Any caller calling `.to_string()` or printing it via `{}` will fail
- Any caller using thiserror's `#[from]` to wrap it needs Display + Error

By comparison, sibling `BackendChangesError<E>` and `BackendSetError<E>` in jmap-server/backend.rs have full Display + Error + source forwarding.

The crate already declares `thiserror = "2"` in Cargo.toml but doesn't use it. Migrate AvailabilityError to:

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum AvailabilityError<E: std::error::Error + 'static> {
    #[error("backend error: {0}")]
    Backend(#[from] E),
    #[error("invalid request: {0}")]
    InvalidRequest(String),
    // ...
}
```

Add `#[non_exhaustive]` to match BackendChangesError pattern.
title: P1: AvailabilityError lacks Display/Error impls — compile-time gap if anyone tries to use ?-operator
